system.name: Pyrocumulus
system.one_liner: a SmartNIC-based hardware hypervisor that live-migrates storage-optimized VMs by intercepting and coordinating I/O without host CPU involvement

components.name: VM
components.role: the virtual machine issuing storage read/write accesses

components.name: Host Software
components.role: host-side software stack containing the hypervisor

components.name: Hypervisor
components.role: software hypervisor mediating VM storage access when host software is on the path

components.name: FPGA SmartNIC
components.role: hardware that can mediate all VM I/O; during LM it acts as a hardware-based hypervisor

components.name: Local Disks
components.role: NVMe storage attached to the host

components.name: NVMe SSD
components.role: individual NVMe disk instances backing Local/Remote Disks

components.name: Source Host
components.role: the host the VM is migrating from, containing its hypervisor and FPGA SmartNIC

components.name: FPGA SmartNIC (Source Host)
components.role: intercepts all VM I/O and initiates LM I/Os directly, bypassing the source host's CPU

components.name: FPGA SmartNIC (Dest. Host)
components.role: receives migration data directly from the source SmartNIC over the network

components.name: Remote Disks
components.role: NVMe storage attached to the destination host receiving migrated data

flows.what: user read/write access mediated by the hypervisor (option 1)
I/O mediated through the SmartNIC before reaching disks (option 1)
mediated I/O reaching local NVMe SSDs (option 1)
native, directly-mapped data path where neither host software nor the SmartNIC sits on the critical path (option 2)
user read/write access on the source host during live migration
consistency write traffic coordinating ongoing VM I/O with LM I/O
data copy traffic transferring migration data directly between SmartNICs, bypassing the source host CPU
migrated data written to the destination host's disks

content.key_idea: Pyrocumulus's FPGA SmartNIC can sit on the common-case I/O path in two configurations (mediating access, or staying off the critical path for directly-mapped storage), and during live migration it becomes a hardware hypervisor that intercepts VM I/O and copies data directly to the destination host's SmartNIC without involving either host's CPU.
content.reading_order: Left to right across three labeled panels: (a) and (b) show the common-case (no LM) data path as a VM-to-disk vertical stack with two user-path options; (c) shows the same stack duplicated across source and destination hosts, linked by a horizontal data-copy arrow, for the live-migration protocol.

both the host software and the SmartNIC are not on the critical path

summary: Figure 3 compares Pyrocumulus's data paths across three panels. In the common case (no live migration), panel (a) shows the FPGA SmartNIC mediating all VM storage I/O between the host software's hypervisor and local NVMe disks, while panel (b) shows an alternative native, directly-mapped path where neither the host software nor the SmartNIC sits on the critical path. Panel (c) shows the protocol used during live migration: the source host's FPGA SmartNIC acts as a hardware-based hypervisor, intercepting VM I/O, sending consistency write traffic to local disks, and copying migration data directly to the destination host's FPGA SmartNIC, which writes it to remote disks, all without involving either host's CPU. A legend distinguishes user read/write access, consistency write traffic, and data copy traffic by arrow style.
summary_zh: 图3对比Pyrocumulus三种数据路径：(a)(b)为无迁移时SmartNIC是否介入VM到本地磁盘的两种方案；(c)为迁移协议，源主机FPGA SmartNIC充当硬件hypervisor，将数据直接拷贝到目的主机，绕过主机CPU。
notes: layout-proposal: repeated layered I/O stack — three comparison panels each stack VM/Host-Software/FPGA-SmartNIC/Local-Disks vertically in the same order, with panel (c) duplicating the stack across source and destination hosts linked by a horizontal data-copy arrow; 'layered' is used as the closest named template but the side-by-side comparison and cross-host duplication go beyond a single layered stack.
